source.text: וְהַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַיְכַסֻּ֨הוּ֙ בַּבְּגָדִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִחַ֖ם לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the king David [was] old, coming in the days; and they covered him with the garments, but not was warm to him.

en.L: And King David [was] old, advanced in days; and they covered him with garments, but he did not get warm.
en.B: King David was now old, well on in years. They covered him with clothes, but he could not keep warm.
en.R: King David was now very old. They covered him with clothes and blankets, but he still could not get warm.

es.L: Y el rey David [era] viejo, entrado en días; y lo cubrían con ropas, pero no entraba en calor.
es.B: El rey David ya era viejo, de edad muy avanzada. Lo cubrían con ropa, pero no lograba entrar en calor.
es.R: El rey David ya era muy anciano. Lo cubrían con ropa y mantas, pero aun así no conseguía calentarse.

fr.L: Et le roi David [était] vieux, avancé en jours ; et on le couvrit de vêtements, mais il ne se réchauffait pas.
fr.B: Le roi David était devenu vieux, chargé d’années. On le couvrait de vêtements, mais il n’arrivait pas à se réchauffer.
fr.R: Le roi David était maintenant très vieux. On le couvrait de vêtements et de couvertures, mais il avait toujours froid.

sw.L: Mfalme Daudi [alikuwa] mzee, aliyeingia katika siku; wakamfunika kwa mavazi, lakini hakupata joto.
sw.B: Mfalme Daudi sasa alikuwa mzee, mwenye miaka mingi. Wakamfunika kwa nguo, lakini hakuweza kupata joto.
sw.R: Mfalme Daudi sasa alikuwa mzee sana. Wakamfunika kwa nguo na mablanketi, lakini bado hakupata joto.

vi.L: Vua Đa-vít [đã] già, tuổi đã cao; người ta đắp áo cho vua, nhưng vua không thấy ấm.
vi.B: Vua Đa-vít bấy giờ đã già, tuổi cao sức yếu. Người ta đắp áo cho vua, nhưng vua vẫn không thấy ấm.
vi.R: Lúc ấy vua Đa-vít đã rất già. Người ta đắp quần áo và chăn mền cho vua, nhưng vua vẫn không thấy ấm.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗 왕은 나이 들어 날들이 많이 [지났다]. 사람들이 옷으로 그를 덮었으나 그는 따뜻해지지 않았다.
ko.B: 다윗 왕은 이제 늙고 나이가 많았다. 사람들이 옷을 덮어 주었으나 그는 몸이 따뜻해지지 않았다.
ko.R: 다윗 왕은 이제 아주 늙었다. 사람들이 옷과 이불을 덮어 주었지만 그는 여전히 몸이 따뜻해지지 않았다.

pt.L: E o rei Davi [estava] velho, avançado em dias; e o cobriam com roupas, mas ele não se aquecia.
pt.B: O rei Davi já estava velho, de idade avançada. Cobriam-no com roupas, mas ele não conseguia se aquecer.
pt.R: O rei Davi estava muito velho. Os seus servos o cobriam com roupas e cobertores, mas mesmo assim ele não conseguia se aquecer.

decisions.choice: coming into the days: advanced in age
decisions.reason: To "come into the days" is a Hebrew way of saying someone is far on in life (Genesis 24:1; Joshua 13:1). David was about seventy at his death (2 Samuel 5:4).

decisions.choice: they covered him: those who looked after him
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It means the people around the king, the servants who speak in verse 2.

decisions.choice: he did not get warm: a sign of failing strength
decisions.reason: The story opens with the king's weakness. The once mighty warrior cannot keep himself warm, and this sets the scene for the struggle over who will follow him.

decisions.choice: well on in years
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a natural English phrase for "coming into the days".

decisions.choice: clothes and blankets
decisions.reason: Readable adds "blankets" because the garments here were bedclothes laid over a man lying down, as verse 2 shows.

decisions.choice: "de edad muy avanzada"
decisions.reason: As the English Balanced (r-en-1): "coming into the days" is said as the ordinary Spanish phrase for great age; Literal keeps "entrado en días".

decisions.choice: passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: As in the French of Samuel, narration is in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and in the passé composé at Readable, with the imparfait for states and repeated actions (here the old king who could not get warm); speeches keep the tenses of speech. Settled for 1 Kings 1-11.

decisions.choice: chargé d'années
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the usual French phrase for great age where Literal keeps "advanced in days".

decisions.choice: mwenye miaka mingi
decisions.reason: Balanced says "mwenye miaka mingi" (of many years), the natural Swahili phrase for the Hebrew "coming into the days"; Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: "tuổi đã cao" (L); "tuổi cao sức yếu" (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "coming into the days" means far on in years (meaning decision); a word-for-word Vietnamese phrase would not be understood, so Literal uses the ordinary phrase for old age.

decisions.choice: "나이 들어 날들이 많이 [지났다]"
decisions.reason: Korean cannot say "coming into the days" as it stands; Literal keeps "days" and supplies the verb in brackets.

decisions.choice: avançado em dias (L); de idade avançada (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of coming into the days (m1) in words a Portuguese reader still understands, since "avançado em anos" is a living phrase; Balanced says "de idade avançada". Readable names "os seus servos" as the subject of the plural verb, the servants who speak in verse 2 (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ ל֣וֹ עֲבָדָ֗יו יְבַקְשׁ֞וּ לַאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה בְתוּלָ֔ה וְעָֽמְדָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּתְהִי־ל֖וֹ סֹכֶ֑נֶת וְשָׁכְבָ֣ה בְחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וְחַ֖ם לַאדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him his servants, let them seek for my lord the king a young woman, a virgin, and she will stand before the king and will be to him a caretaker, and she will lie in your bosom, and will be warm to my lord the king.

en.L: And his servants said to him, "Let them seek for my lord the king a young woman, a virgin, and let her stand before the king and be a caretaker to him, and let her lie in your bosom, and my lord the king will get warm."
en.B: So his officials said to him, "Let a young virgin be found for my lord the king, to wait on the king and look after him. Let her lie in your arms, so that my lord the king may keep warm."
en.R: So his officials said to him, "Your Majesty, let us look for a young woman, a virgin. She can serve you and take care of you. She can lie close beside you and keep you warm."

es.L: Y le dijeron sus siervos: «Busquen para mi señor el rey una joven, una virgen, y que esté delante del rey y le sea cuidadora, y que se acueste en tu seno, y mi señor el rey entrará en calor».
es.B: Entonces sus oficiales le dijeron: «Que se busque para mi señor el rey una joven virgen, que atienda al rey y lo cuide. Que se acueste en tus brazos, para que mi señor el rey se mantenga caliente».
es.R: Entonces sus oficiales le dijeron: «Mi rey, permítenos buscar una muchacha joven, una virgen. Ella podrá servirte y cuidarte. Podrá acostarse a tu lado y darte calor».

fr.L: Et ses serviteurs lui dirent : « Qu’on cherche pour mon seigneur le roi une jeune fille, une vierge, et qu’elle se tienne devant le roi et lui soit une garde-malade, et qu’elle couche dans ton sein, et mon seigneur le roi se réchauffera. »
fr.B: Ses officiers lui dirent alors : « Qu’on cherche pour mon seigneur le roi une jeune fille vierge, qui se tiendra au service du roi et prendra soin de lui. Elle couchera dans tes bras, et mon seigneur le roi aura chaud. »
fr.R: Alors ses officiers lui ont dit : « Ô roi, laisse-nous chercher une jeune fille, une vierge. Elle pourra te servir et s’occuper de toi. Elle se couchera tout près de toi et te tiendra chaud. »

sw.L: Watumishi wake wakamwambia, "Na wamtafutie bwana wangu mfalme msichana, bikira, naye asimame mbele ya mfalme na kuwa mtunzaji wake, naye alale kifuani pako, ili bwana wangu mfalme apate joto."
sw.B: Basi maafisa wake wakamwambia, "Bwana wangu mfalme na atafutiwe msichana bikira, amhudumie mfalme na kumtunza. Alale mikononi mwako, ili bwana wangu mfalme apate joto."
sw.R: Basi maafisa wake wakamwambia, "Mtukufu mfalme, turuhusu tukutafutie msichana bikira. Atakuhudumia na kukutunza. Atalala karibu nawe na kukupa joto."

vi.L: Các đầy tớ của vua nói với vua: "Xin cho người ta tìm cho chúa tôi là vua một thiếu nữ còn trinh, để nàng đứng hầu trước mặt vua và làm người chăm sóc vua; nàng sẽ nằm trong lòng vua, và chúa tôi là vua sẽ được ấm."
vi.B: Vì vậy, các quần thần tâu với vua: "Xin cho tìm một trinh nữ trẻ cho bệ hạ, để nàng hầu hạ và chăm sóc bệ hạ. Nàng sẽ nằm trong vòng tay bệ hạ để bệ hạ được ấm."
vi.R: Vì vậy, các quần thần thưa với vua: "Thưa đức vua, chúng tôi xin đi tìm một thiếu nữ còn trinh. Cô ấy sẽ hầu hạ và chăm sóc đức vua. Cô ấy sẽ nằm sát bên đức vua để giữ ấm cho đức vua."

ko.L: 그의 신하들이 그에게 말했다. "내 주 임금님을 위하여 젊은 여자, 처녀 하나를 찾게 하십시오. 그 여자가 임금님 앞에 서서 그분의 시중을 들고, 임금님의 품에 누워 내 주 임금님께서 따뜻해지시게 하십시오."
ko.B: 그래서 신하들이 왕에게 말했다. "내 주 임금님을 위하여 젊은 처녀를 하나 찾아서 임금님을 모시고 돌보게 하십시오. 그 여자가 임금님의 품에 누워 내 주 임금님께서 따뜻하게 지내시도록 하십시오."
ko.R: 그래서 신하들이 왕에게 말했다. "임금님, 저희가 젊은 처녀를 하나 찾아보겠습니다. 그 여자가 임금님을 모시고 돌보아 드릴 것입니다. 임금님 곁에 누워서 몸을 따뜻하게 해 드릴 것입니다."

pt.L: E os seus servos lhe disseram: "Que procurem para o meu senhor, o rei, uma moça virgem, e que ela fique diante do rei e seja para ele uma cuidadora; e que ela se deite no seu colo, e o meu senhor, o rei, se aquecerá."
pt.B: Por isso os seus oficiais lhe disseram: "Que se procure uma jovem virgem para o meu senhor, o rei, para servir o rei e cuidar dele. Que ela se deite nos seus braços, para que o meu senhor, o rei, se aqueça."
pt.R: Então os seus oficiais lhe disseram: "Majestade, deixe-nos procurar uma moça, uma virgem. Ela pode servir e cuidar do senhor. Ela pode se deitar bem junto do senhor e mantê-lo aquecido."

decisions.choice: caretaker: one who looks after and tends someone
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It comes from a verb meaning "to be of use, to serve", and here it names a woman who waits on the old king and cares for him. It does not mean a wife.

decisions.choice: stand before the king: serve him
decisions.reason: To "stand before" someone of rank is to wait on him and be at his service (1 Samuel 16:21-22).

decisions.choice: lie in your bosom: lie close to keep him warm
decisions.reason: The purpose the servants give is warmth: a young person's body heat for a cold old man. The phrase can also be used of a wife (2 Samuel 12:8), but verse 4 says plainly that there were no sexual relations.

decisions.choice: my lord the king: the polite way to speak to a king
decisions.reason: Courtiers speak of the king in the third person, "my lord the king", even while speaking to him, and then switch to "you" ("your bosom"). The switch is natural in Hebrew court speech.

decisions.choice: his officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants (*'avadim*) are his court officials. As elsewhere in Samuel and Kings, Literal says "servants" and Balanced and Readable say "officials".

decisions.choice: Your Majesty; you
decisions.reason: Readable uses a modern form of address to a king and speaks to him as "you" throughout, as in 1 Samuel 17:55.

decisions.choice: "siervos" (L); "oficiales" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for the king's servants, kept for Kings: Literal "siervos", Balanced and Readable "oficiales", the men of the court (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "mi señor el rey" (L, B); "Mi rey" (R) with "tú"
decisions.reason: Courtiers speak to the king with "tú", as the Samuel notes set for Spanish; respect is carried by "mi señor el rey". Where the English Readable says "Your Majesty" (r-en-2), Spanish says "mi rey", since "Majestad" would need "usted".

decisions.choice: serviteurs (L); officiers (B, R)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his court officials: "serviteurs" at Literal, "officiers" at Balanced and Readable, as in the French of Samuel. Settled for 1 Kings 1-11.

decisions.choice: Ô roi; tu
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "Your Majesty", French says "ô roi" and keeps "tu", as in Samuel: "Majesté" would call for "vous". Settled for 1 Kings 1-11.

decisions.choice: watumishi (Literal); maafisa (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his court officials. As in the Swahili of Samuel, Literal says "watumishi" and Balanced and Readable "maafisa"; used through this block.

decisions.choice: Mtukufu mfalme
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "Your Majesty", Swahili Readable says "Mtukufu mfalme" and speaks to the king as "wewe", as in 2 Samuel 14; Literal and Balanced keep "bwana wangu mfalme".

decisions.choice: "chúa tôi là vua" (L); "bệ hạ" (B); "đức vua" (R), with "tâu" / "thưa" for speaking to the king
decisions.reason: As the Kings terms note sets for these books: subjects address the king in the third person with these forms, which also carry the Hebrew switch from "my lord the king" to "you"; kept through this block.

decisions.choice: "các đầy tớ" (L); "các quần thần" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his court officials (English decision); Vietnamese "quần thần" names them, as in Samuel.

decisions.choice: Subjects speak to the king in 합쇼체, calling him "내 주 임금님" (L, B) or "임금님" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note, for the whole of 1 Kings 1-11: the courtiers' respect is carried by the honorific endings and the title, not by a pronoun.

decisions.choice: "신하들"
decisions.reason: The king's servants here are his court officials; Korean says 신하들, as in Samuel.

decisions.choice: o meu senhor, o rei; o seu colo (L, B); Majestade, o senhor (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel 1:10, 9:11 and 14:4 in Portuguese: subjects speak to the king in the courtly third person, "o meu senhor, o rei", with "o seu" and "o senhor" where the Hebrew turns to "you" (m4), and with "o seu servo", "a sua serva" where it has them; Readable says "Majestade" and "o senhor", as the English says "Your Majesty". "Vossa Majestade" would bring in the "vós" forms Brazilian Portuguese no longer uses. The king answers with "você" and "vocês".

decisions.choice: os seus servos (L); os seus oficiais (B, R); cuidadora (L)
decisions.reason: The king's servants at court are "servos" at Literal and "oficiais" at Balanced and Readable, as 2 Samuel 3:38 sets them in Portuguese. "Cuidadora" names a woman who looks after someone (m1) without making her a wife or a hired nurse.

source.text: וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה יָפָ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּמְצְא֗וּ אֶת־אֲבִישַׁג֙ הַשּׁ֣וּנַמִּ֔ית וַיָּבִ֥אוּ אֹתָ֖הּ לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sought a young woman beautiful in all [the] territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

en.L: And they sought a beautiful young woman in all the territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
en.B: So they searched throughout the land of Israel for a beautiful young woman. They found Abishag the Shunammite, and they brought her to the king.
en.R: So they looked all over Israel for a beautiful young woman. They found Abishag, from the town of Shunem, and brought her to the king.

es.L: Y buscaron una joven hermosa en todo el territorio de Israel, y hallaron a Abisag la sunamita y la trajeron al rey.
es.B: Así que buscaron por todo el territorio de Israel una joven hermosa. Encontraron a Abisag la sunamita, y se la llevaron al rey.
es.R: Buscaron por todo Israel una muchacha hermosa. Encontraron a Abisag, del pueblo de Sunem, y se la llevaron al rey.

fr.L: Et on chercha une belle jeune fille dans tout le territoire d’Israël, et on trouva Abishag la Shounamite, et on l’amena au roi.
fr.B: On chercha donc dans tout le pays d’Israël une belle jeune fille. On trouva Abishag la Shounamite, et on l’amena au roi.
fr.R: On a donc cherché dans tout Israël une belle jeune fille. On a trouvé Abishag, qui venait de la ville de Shounem, et on l’a amenée au roi.

sw.L: Wakamtafuta msichana mzuri katika nchi yote ya Israeli, wakampata Abishagi Mshunami, wakamleta kwa mfalme.
sw.B: Basi wakatafuta katika nchi yote ya Israeli msichana mzuri. Wakampata Abishagi Mshunami, wakamleta kwa mfalme.
sw.R: Basi walitafuta kila mahali katika Israeli msichana mzuri. Wakampata Abishagi, wa mji wa Shunemu, wakamleta kwa mfalme.

vi.L: Người ta tìm một thiếu nữ xinh đẹp trong khắp lãnh thổ Y-sơ-ra-ên, và tìm được A-bi-sác người Su-nem, rồi đưa nàng đến với vua.
vi.B: Vậy người ta tìm khắp đất Y-sơ-ra-ên một thiếu nữ xinh đẹp. Họ tìm được A-bi-sác người Su-nem và đưa nàng đến với vua.
vi.R: Vậy họ đi tìm khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên một thiếu nữ xinh đẹp. Họ tìm được A-bi-sác, quê ở thành Su-nem, và đưa cô đến với vua.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 이스라엘 온 지역에서 아름다운 젊은 여자를 찾다가 수넴 여자 아비삭을 찾아내어 그 여자를 왕에게 데려왔다.
ko.B: 그래서 그들은 이스라엘 온 땅을 두루 다니며 아름다운 젊은 여자를 찾았다. 그들은 수넴 여자 아비삭을 찾아내어 왕에게 데려왔다.
ko.R: 그래서 그들은 이스라엘 전체를 돌아다니며 아름다운 젊은 여자를 찾았다. 그들은 수넴 마을에서 온 아비삭을 찾아내어 왕에게 데려왔다.

pt.L: E procuraram uma moça bonita em todo o território de Israel, e encontraram Abisague, a sunamita, e a trouxeram ao rei.
pt.B: Então procuraram por toda a terra de Israel uma moça bonita. Encontraram Abisague, a sunamita, e a levaram ao rei.
pt.R: Então procuraram em todo o Israel uma moça bonita. Encontraram Abisague, da cidade de Suném, e a levaram ao rei.

decisions.choice: Abishag the Shunammite: a woman from Shunem
decisions.reason: Shunem was a town in the territory of Issachar, in the Jezreel valley (Joshua 19:18; 1 Samuel 28:4; 2 Kings 4:8). Abishag matters again in 2:13-25, where Adonijah asks to marry her.

decisions.choice: in all the territory of Israel: a wide search
decisions.reason: The search went through the whole land, which shows the care taken to find the most fitting young woman for the king.

decisions.choice: from the town of Shunem
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "Shunammite".

decisions.choice: "Abisag la sunamita" (L, B); "Abisag, del pueblo de Sunem" (R)
decisions.reason: The name follows the Kings terms note; "sunamita" is the usual Spanish gentilic of Sunem, and Readable names the town as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: Abishag la Shounamite; Shounem
decisions.reason: The forms of the terms note and of the French Samuel (Shounem, 1 Samuel 28:4); kept for 1 and 2 Kings.

decisions.choice: Abisague, a sunamita (L, B); Abisague, da cidade de Suném (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 1:15; 2:17-22): the name takes its usual Brazilian form, with the final "-e" Portuguese adds after a consonant, as "Joabe"; "sunamita" is formed from "Suném", the town of Joshua 19:18 and 1 Samuel 28:4 in Portuguese (m1), which Readable names, as the English does.

source.text: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה יָפָ֣ה עַד־מְאֹ֑ד וַתְּהִ֨י לַמֶּ֤לֶךְ סֹכֶ֨נֶת֙ וַתְּשָׁ֣רְתֵ֔הוּ וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א יְדָעָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the young woman [was] beautiful to very [much], and she was to the king a caretaker, and she served him; and the king not knew her.

en.L: And the young woman [was] very beautiful; and she became a caretaker to the king and served him, but the king did not know her.
en.B: The young woman was very beautiful. She looked after the king and waited on him, but the king had no sexual relations with her.
en.R: She was very beautiful. She took care of the king and served him, but the king did not have sexual relations with her.

es.L: Y la joven [era] hermosa en gran manera; y fue cuidadora del rey y le servía, pero el rey no la conoció.
es.B: La joven era muy hermosa. Ella cuidaba al rey y lo atendía, pero el rey no tuvo relaciones sexuales con ella.
es.R: Era muy hermosa. Ella cuidaba al rey y lo servía, pero el rey no tuvo relaciones sexuales con ella.

fr.L: Et la jeune fille [était] belle extrêmement ; et elle fut pour le roi une garde-malade et le servit, mais le roi ne la connut pas.
fr.B: La jeune fille était très belle. Elle prenait soin du roi et le servait, mais le roi n’eut pas de relations avec elle.
fr.R: Elle était très belle. Elle s’occupait du roi et le servait, mais le roi n’a pas eu de relations sexuelles avec elle.

sw.L: Msichana huyo [alikuwa] mzuri sana; akawa mtunzaji wa mfalme, akamhudumia, lakini mfalme hakumjua.
sw.B: Msichana huyo alikuwa mzuri sana. Akamtunza mfalme na kumhudumia, lakini mfalme hakulala naye.
sw.R: Alikuwa mzuri sana. Alimtunza mfalme na kumhudumia, lakini mfalme hakufanya naye tendo la ndoa.

vi.L: Thiếu nữ ấy rất xinh đẹp; nàng làm người chăm sóc vua và hầu hạ vua, nhưng vua không biết nàng.
vi.B: Thiếu nữ ấy rất xinh đẹp. Nàng chăm sóc và hầu hạ vua, nhưng vua không ăn nằm với nàng.
vi.R: Cô rất xinh đẹp. Cô chăm sóc và phục vụ vua, nhưng vua không ăn nằm với cô.

ko.L: 그리고 그 젊은 여자는 매우 아름다웠다. 그 여자는 왕의 시중드는 사람이 되어 그를 섬겼으나, 왕은 그 여자를 알지 않았다.
ko.B: 그 젊은 여자는 매우 아름다웠다. 그 여자는 왕을 돌보며 시중을 들었으나, 왕은 그 여자와 잠자리를 같이하지 않았다.
ko.R: 아비삭은 매우 아름다웠다. 그 여자는 왕을 돌보며 섬겼지만, 왕은 그 여자와 잠자리를 하지 않았다.

pt.L: E a moça [era] muito bonita; e ela se tornou cuidadora do rei e o servia, mas o rei não a conheceu.
pt.B: A moça era muito bonita. Ela cuidava do rei e o servia, mas o rei não teve relações com ela.
pt.R: Ela era muito bonita. Cuidava do rei e o servia, mas o rei não teve relações sexuais com ela.

decisions.choice: did not know her: had no sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: To "know" a woman is a Hebrew way of speaking of sexual relations (Genesis 4:1; 1 Samuel 1:19). The narrator says plainly that Abishag became the king's nurse and servant, not his wife in the full sense.

decisions.choice: caretaker: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The same rare word as in verse 2: a woman who tends and looks after him.

decisions.choice: the king did not know her: a sign of his weakness, and of Abishag's standing
decisions.reason: In a story about who will rule, the remark shows how weak David has become. It also explains her position later: she lived as part of the king's household but was not his wife (2:17-22).

decisions.choice: know
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: "no la conoció"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "know" for sexual relations, as the English Literal does (r-en-1); Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: hakulala naye (Balanced); hakufanya naye tendo la ndoa (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "hakumjua" (did not know her); Balanced uses the usual polite Swahili "hakulala naye", and Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "không biết nàng" (L); "không ăn nằm với nàng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom, as the English does; Balanced and Readable say what it means with the usual Vietnamese phrase.

source.text: וַאֲדֹנִיָּ֧ה בֶן־חַגִּ֛ית מִתְנַשֵּׂ֥א לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י אֶמְלֹ֑ךְ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ ל֗וֹ רֶ֚כֶב וּפָ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ רָצִ֥ים לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And Adonijah son of Haggith [was] lifting himself up, saying, I will reign; and he made for himself chariot and horsemen, and fifty men running before him.

en.L: And Adonijah son of Haggith [was] exalting himself, saying, "I will reign." And he made for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men running before him.
en.B: Now Adonijah son of Haggith was putting himself forward, saying, "I will be king." He got himself chariots and horsemen, with fifty men to run ahead of him.
en.R: Meanwhile Adonijah, the son of David's wife Haggith, was boasting, "I am going to be king!" He got chariots and horsemen for himself, and fifty men to run in front of him.

es.L: Y Adonías hijo de Haguit se enaltecía, diciendo: «Yo reinaré». Y se hizo de carros y jinetes, y cincuenta hombres que corrían delante de él.
es.B: Mientras tanto, Adonías hijo de Haguit se daba importancia, diciendo: «Yo seré rey». Se consiguió carros y jinetes, y cincuenta hombres que corrieran delante de él.
es.R: Mientras tanto, Adonías, el hijo de Haguit, esposa de David, se jactaba: «¡Yo voy a ser rey!». Consiguió carros de guerra y jinetes para sí, y cincuenta hombres que corrieran delante de él.

fr.L: Et Adonias fils de Haggith s’élevait, disant : « Moi, je régnerai. » Et il se fit faire des chars et des cavaliers, et cinquante hommes qui couraient devant lui.
fr.B: Or Adonias, fils de Haggith, se mettait en avant et disait : « C’est moi qui serai roi. » Il se procura des chars et des cavaliers, et cinquante hommes pour courir devant lui.
fr.R: Pendant ce temps, Adonias, le fils de Haggith, une des femmes de David, se vantait : « C’est moi qui vais être roi ! » Il s’est procuré des chars et des cavaliers, et cinquante hommes pour courir devant lui.

sw.L: Na Adoniya mwana wa Hagithi [alikuwa] akijikweza, akisema, "Mimi nitatawala." Akajifanyia magari ya vita na wapanda farasi, na watu hamsini wakikimbia mbele yake.
sw.B: Wakati huo Adoniya mwana wa Hagithi alikuwa akijitanguliza, akisema, "Nitakuwa mfalme." Akajipatia magari ya vita na wapanda farasi, pamoja na watu hamsini wa kukimbia mbele yake.
sw.R: Wakati huo Adoniya, mwana wa Hagithi mke wa Daudi, alikuwa akijigamba, "Mimi nitakuwa mfalme!" Akajipatia magari ya vita na wapanda farasi, na watu hamsini wa kukimbia mbele yake.

vi.L: Bấy giờ A-đô-ni-gia con trai Ha-ghít [đang] tự tôn mình lên mà nói: "Ta sẽ làm vua." Ông sắm cho mình xe chiến mã và kỵ binh, cùng năm mươi người chạy trước mặt mình.
vi.B: Trong khi đó, A-đô-ni-gia con trai bà Ha-ghít tự đề cao mình mà nói: "Ta sẽ làm vua." Ông sắm cho mình xe chiến mã và kỵ binh, cùng năm mươi người chạy trước mặt.
vi.R: Trong khi đó, A-đô-ni-gia, con trai của Ha-ghít, vợ vua Đa-vít, khoe khoang: "Ta sẽ làm vua!" Ông sắm cho mình xe ngựa và kỵ binh, cùng năm mươi người chạy phía trước mình.

ko.L: 그리고 학깃의 아들 아도니야가 스스로 높이며 "내가 왕이 되겠다" 하고 말했다. 그리고 그는 자기를 위해 병거와 기병, 그리고 자기 앞에서 달릴 사람 쉰 명을 마련했다.
ko.B: 그때 학깃의 아들 아도니야가 "내가 왕이 될 것이다" 하며 자기를 내세웠다. 그는 병거와 기병을 마련하고, 자기 앞에서 달릴 호위병 쉰 명을 두었다.
ko.R: 그 무렵 다윗의 아내 학깃이 낳은 아들 아도니야가 "내가 왕이 될 거다!" 하고 뽐내고 다녔다. 그는 병거와 기병을 마련하고, 자기 앞에서 달릴 사람 쉰 명도 두었다.

pt.L: E Adonias, filho de Hagite, se exaltava, dizendo: "Eu reinarei." E fez para si carros e cavaleiros, e cinquenta homens que corriam diante dele.
pt.B: Enquanto isso, Adonias, filho de Hagite, se promovia, dizendo: "Eu serei rei." Ele arranjou carros e cavaleiros, e cinquenta homens para correr à sua frente.
pt.R: Nesse tempo, Adonias, filho de Davi e de Hagite, se gabava: "Eu vou ser rei!" Ele arranjou carros de guerra e cavaleiros, e cinquenta homens para correr na frente dele.

decisions.choice: Adonijah son of Haggith: David's fourth son, now the eldest living
decisions.reason: Adonijah was born at Hebron (2 Samuel 3:4). Amnon and Absalom, the first and third sons, were dead (2 Samuel 13:28-29; 18:14-15), and Chileab, the second, is not heard of again. So by age Adonijah was next in line.

decisions.choice: exalting himself: an ongoing claim
decisions.reason: The verb describes a continuing action: he was raising himself up, setting himself forward as the heir.

decisions.choice: chariots, horsemen and runners: the display of a would-be king
decisions.reason: Absalom did the same when he reached for the throne (2 Samuel 15:1), and Samuel had warned that a king would have men run before his chariots (1 Samuel 8:11).

decisions.choice: David's wife Haggith
decisions.reason: Readable says who Haggith was.

decisions.choice: chariots
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is singular but stands for chariots as a group.

decisions.choice: "carros" (L, B); "carros de guerra" (R)
decisions.reason: The collective singular is plural in Spanish, as in English (r-en-2); "carros y jinetes" is the Kings terms note's pair. Haguit is the usual Spanish form of Haggith, as in 2 Samuel 3:4.

decisions.choice: "xe chiến mã và kỵ binh" (L, B); "xe ngựa và kỵ binh" (R)
decisions.reason: The Kings terms note's phrase for chariots and horsemen; Readable uses the plainer "xe ngựa".

decisions.choice: "병거와 기병"
decisions.reason: As the Kings and Chronicles terms note: 병거 for the war chariot at every level in these books, so the regnal and battle passages use one word.

decisions.choice: Adonias, filho de Hagite
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the names as 2 Samuel 3:4 has them in Portuguese, "Adonias" in the form Brazilian readers know and "Hagite" with the final "-e" Portuguese adds after a consonant. Readable says "filho de Davi e de Hagite" for the English "the son of David's wife Haggith", which says who she was without a long apposition.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־עֲצָב֨וֹ אָבִ֤יו מִיָּמָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַדּ֖וּעַ כָּ֣כָה עָשִׂ֑יתָ וְגַם־ה֤וּא טֽוֹב־תֹּ֨אַר֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְאֹת֥וֹ יָלְדָ֖ה אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And not pained him his father from his days, saying, why thus have you done? And also he [was] good of form very, and him she bore after Absalom.

en.L: And his father had not pained him [any of] his days, saying, "Why have you done thus?" And he also [was] very good of form, and she bore him after Absalom.
en.B: His father had never once crossed him by asking, "Why have you done this?" He was also very handsome, and he was born next after Absalom.
en.R: His father David had never scolded him or asked, "Why are you doing that?" Adonijah was also very handsome. He was born after Absalom.

es.L: Y su padre no lo había entristecido en todos sus días, diciendo: «¿Por qué has hecho así?». Y también él [era] muy hermoso de apariencia, y [ella] lo dio a luz después de Absalón.
es.B: Su padre nunca lo había contrariado preguntándole: «¿Por qué has hecho esto?». Además era muy bien parecido, y había nacido después de Absalón.
es.R: Su padre David nunca lo había regañado ni le había preguntado: «¿Por qué haces eso?». Adonías también era muy guapo. Había nacido después de Absalón.

fr.L: Et son père ne l’avait pas contrarié de ses jours, disant : « Pourquoi as-tu fait ainsi ? » Et lui aussi [était] très beau de forme, et elle l’avait enfanté après Absalom.
fr.B: Jamais son père ne l’avait contrarié en lui demandant : « Pourquoi agis-tu ainsi ? » Il était en outre très beau, et il était né après Absalom.
fr.R: Son père David ne l’avait jamais grondé ; il ne lui avait jamais demandé : « Pourquoi fais-tu cela ? » Adonias était aussi très beau. Il était né après Absalom.

sw.L: Na baba yake hakuwa amemhuzunisha [hata siku moja ya] siku zake, akisema, "Kwa nini umefanya hivi?" Naye pia [alikuwa] mzuri sana wa umbo, naye [mama yake] alimzaa baada ya Absalomu.
sw.B: Baba yake hakuwahi kumkemea hata mara moja kwa kumwuliza, "Kwa nini umefanya hivi?" Tena alikuwa mzuri sana wa sura, naye alizaliwa baada ya Absalomu.
sw.R: Baba yake Daudi hakuwahi kumkaripia wala kumwuliza, "Kwa nini unafanya hivyo?" Adoniya pia alikuwa mzuri sana wa sura. Alizaliwa baada ya Absalomu.

vi.L: Cha ông chưa hề làm ông buồn lòng [trong] suốt đời ông mà nói: "Sao con làm như vậy?" Ông cũng rất đẹp dáng, và bà đã sinh ông sau Áp-sa-lôm.
vi.B: Cha ông chưa từng một lần trách ông rằng: "Sao con làm như thế?" Ông lại rất khôi ngô, và được sinh ra kế sau Áp-sa-lôm.
vi.R: Vua Đa-vít, cha ông, chưa bao giờ rầy la ông hay hỏi: "Sao con làm như thế?" A-đô-ni-gia cũng rất đẹp trai. Ông sinh ra sau Áp-sa-lôm.

ko.L: 그의 아버지는 그가 사는 날 동안 "너는 왜 이렇게 했느냐?" 하고 말하며 그를 언짢게 한 적이 없었다. 그리고 그도 용모가 매우 좋았으며, [그의 어머니가] 압살롬 다음에 그를 낳았다.
ko.B: 그의 아버지는 "너는 왜 이런 짓을 했느냐?" 하고 물으며 그를 한 번도 꾸짖은 적이 없었다. 그는 또한 용모가 매우 뛰어났고, 압살롬 다음으로 태어난 아들이었다.
ko.R: 그의 아버지 다윗은 "너는 왜 그런 일을 하느냐?" 하고 그를 꾸짖거나 물은 적이 한 번도 없었다. 아도니야는 또 아주 잘생겼다. 그는 압살롬 다음에 태어났다.

pt.L: E o seu pai não o tinha magoado [em nenhum] dos seus dias, dizendo: "Por que você fez assim?" E também ele [era] de muito boa aparência, e [ela] o tinha dado à luz depois de Absalão.
pt.B: O seu pai nunca o tinha contrariado, nem uma vez, perguntando: "Por que você fez isso?" Ele também era muito bonito e tinha nascido logo depois de Absalão.
pt.R: O seu pai Davi nunca o repreendeu nem perguntou: "Por que você está fazendo isso?" Adonias também era muito bonito. Ele nasceu depois de Absalão.

decisions.choice: pained him: crossed or rebuked him
decisions.reason: The verb means to hurt or grieve. Here it means David never upset his son by correcting him. The same lack of discipline is seen with Amnon and Absalom (2 Samuel 13:21; 14:33).

decisions.choice: she bore him: his mother, Haggith
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine with no named subject. It means Adonijah's mother bore him; he was the next son born after Absalom, though to a different mother (2 Samuel 3:3-4).

decisions.choice: very handsome: like Absalom
decisions.reason: Absalom too was praised for his looks (2 Samuel 14:25), as Saul was before him (1 Samuel 9:2). Good looks and a father who let him have his way echo the story of the earlier rebel son.

decisions.choice: crossed him
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain verb for the father's hurting or correcting.

decisions.choice: His father David
decisions.reason: Readable names the father.

decisions.choice: "lo había contrariado"
decisions.reason: Balanced says "contrariar", to cross someone's will, for the Hebrew "pain" (r-en-1); Literal keeps "entristecido".

decisions.choice: [mama yake] alimzaa
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is feminine with no named subject; Swahili verb prefixes do not show gender, so Literal supplies "[mama yake]" (his mother) to keep the sense the Hebrew marks.

decisions.choice: "[그의 어머니가]"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb "she bore" has a feminine subject; Korean has no feminine verb form, so Literal supplies the mother in brackets.

decisions.choice: magoado (L); contrariado (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to hurt or grieve (m1): Literal says "magoado"; Balanced says "contrariado", which is what the hurt was here, a father crossing his son. David says "você" to his son, as fathers do in Samuel. "Absalão" as 2 Samuel.

source.text: וַיִּהְי֣וּ דְבָרָ֔יו עִ֚ם יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֔ה וְעִ֖ם אֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וַֽיַּעְזְר֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And were his words with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they helped after Adonijah.

en.L: And his words were with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they helped after Adonijah.
en.B: He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they gave Adonijah their support.
en.R: Adonijah made plans with Joab, the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest, and they agreed to support him.

es.L: Y sus palabras estaban con Joab hijo de Sarvia y con Abiatar el sacerdote, y ellos ayudaban siguiendo a Adonías.
es.B: Adonías se puso de acuerdo con Joab hijo de Sarvia y con el sacerdote Abiatar, y ellos le dieron su apoyo.
es.R: Adonías hizo planes con Joab, el hijo de Sarvia, y con Abiatar el sacerdote, y ellos aceptaron apoyarlo.

fr.L: Et ses paroles furent avec Joab fils de Tserouya et avec Abiathar le prêtre, et ils aidèrent à la suite d’Adonias.
fr.B: Il se concerta avec Joab, fils de Tserouya, et avec le prêtre Abiathar, et ceux-ci prirent le parti d’Adonias.
fr.R: Adonias a fait des plans avec Joab, le fils de Tserouya, et avec le prêtre Abiathar, et ils ont accepté de le soutenir.

sw.L: Maneno yake yakawa pamoja na Yoabu mwana wa Seruya na pamoja na Abiathari kuhani, nao wakamsaidia Adoniya kwa kumfuata.
sw.B: Akashauriana na Yoabu mwana wa Seruya na Abiathari kuhani, nao wakamuunga mkono Adoniya.
sw.R: Adoniya akapanga mambo pamoja na Yoabu mwana wa Seruya na Abiathari kuhani, nao wakakubali kumuunga mkono.

vi.L: Ông bàn bạc với Giô-áp con trai Xê-ru-gia và với thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha, và họ giúp đỡ theo A-đô-ni-gia.
vi.B: Ông bàn bạc với Giô-áp con trai Xê-ru-gia và với thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha, và họ ủng hộ A-đô-ni-gia.
vi.R: A-đô-ni-gia bàn tính với Giô-áp, con trai bà Xê-ru-gia, và với thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha. Hai người này đồng ý ủng hộ ông.

ko.L: 그리고 그의 말이 스루야의 아들 요압과 제사장 아비아달과 함께 있었고, 그들은 아도니야를 따라 도왔다.
ko.B: 아도니야는 스루야의 아들 요압과 제사장 아비아달과 의논했고, 그들은 아도니야를 지지했다.
ko.R: 아도니야는 스루야의 아들 요압과 제사장 아비아달과 함께 계획을 세웠고, 그들은 아도니야를 돕기로 했다.

pt.L: E as suas palavras estavam com Joabe, filho de Zeruia, e com Abiatar, o sacerdote, e eles ajudavam, seguindo Adonias.
pt.B: Ele combinou os seus planos com Joabe, filho de Zeruia, e com Abiatar, o sacerdote, e eles deram o seu apoio a Adonias.
pt.R: Adonias fez planos com Joabe, filho de Zeruia, e com o sacerdote Abiatar, e eles concordaram em apoiá-lo.

decisions.choice: his words were with: he conferred with them
decisions.reason: To have one's words with someone is to talk things over with him, to plan together.

decisions.choice: helped after: followed and supported
decisions.reason: "Helped after Adonijah" means they took his side and gave him their help.

decisions.choice: Joab and Abiathar: the army commander and a priest of long standing
decisions.reason: Joab was David's nephew and the commander of his army (2 Samuel 8:16). Abiathar had been with David since Saul's days (1 Samuel 22:20-23) and served with Zadok as priest (2 Samuel 15:24-29). Adonijah had the army and part of the priesthood on his side.

decisions.choice: "bàn bạc với" (L, B)
decisions.reason: "His words were with" means he conferred with them (meaning decision); a word-for-word Vietnamese phrase has no sense, so every level says "bàn bạc".

decisions.choice: ajudavam, seguindo Adonias
decisions.reason: Portuguese "ajudar atrás de" would mean nothing, so Literal joins the two words of the idiom (m2) as "ajudavam, seguindo", which keeps both the help and the following.

source.text: וְצָד֣וֹק הַ֠כֹּהֵן וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע וְנָתָ֤ן הַנָּבִיא֙ וְשִׁמְעִ֣י וְרֵעִ֔י וְהַגִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑ד לֹ֥א הָי֖וּ עִם־אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: But Zadok the priest and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and Nathan the prophet and Shimei and Rei and the mighty men who [were] to David not were with Adonijah.

en.L: But Zadok the priest and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and Nathan the prophet and Shimei and Rei and the mighty men who [belonged] to David were not with Adonijah.
en.B: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei and David's own warriors did not side with Adonijah.
en.R: But others did not join Adonijah. They were Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's own warriors.

es.L: Pero Sadoc el sacerdote y Benaía hijo de Joiada y Natán el profeta y Simei y Rei y los valientes que [eran] de David no estaban con Adonías.
es.B: Pero el sacerdote Sadoc, Benaía hijo de Joiada, el profeta Natán, Simei, Rei y los guerreros de David no se pusieron de parte de Adonías.
es.R: Pero otros no se unieron a Adonías. Eran Sadoc el sacerdote, Benaía hijo de Joiada, Natán el profeta, Simei, Rei y los guerreros de David.

fr.L: Mais Sadok le prêtre, et Benaya fils de Yehoyada, et Nathan le prophète, et Shiméï, et Réï, et les vaillants hommes qui [étaient] à David n’étaient pas avec Adonias.
fr.B: Mais le prêtre Sadok, Benaya fils de Yehoyada, le prophète Nathan, Shiméï, Réï et les guerriers de David ne se rangèrent pas du côté d’Adonias.
fr.R: Mais d’autres ne se sont pas joints à Adonias : le prêtre Sadok, Benaya, le fils de Yehoyada, le prophète Nathan, Shiméï, Réï, et les guerriers de David.

sw.L: Lakini Sadoki kuhani na Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada na Nathani nabii na Shimei na Rei na mashujaa waliokuwa wa Daudi hawakuwa pamoja na Adoniya.
sw.B: Lakini Sadoki kuhani, Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada, Nathani nabii, Shimei, Rei na mashujaa wa Daudi mwenyewe hawakumuunga mkono Adoniya.
sw.R: Lakini wengine hawakujiunga na Adoniya. Hao walikuwa Sadoki kuhani, Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada, Nathani nabii, Shimei, Rei na mashujaa wa Daudi mwenyewe.

vi.L: Nhưng thầy tế lễ Xa-đốc, Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa, nhà tiên tri Na-than, Si-mê-i, Rê-i và các dũng sĩ thuộc về Đa-vít không theo A-đô-ni-gia.
vi.B: Nhưng thầy tế lễ Xa-đốc, Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa, nhà tiên tri Na-than, Si-mê-i, Rê-i và các chiến binh riêng của Đa-vít không theo phe A-đô-ni-gia.
vi.R: Nhưng có những người không theo A-đô-ni-gia. Đó là thầy tế lễ Xa-đốc, Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa, nhà tiên tri Na-than, Si-mê-i, Rê-i và các chiến binh riêng của Đa-vít.

ko.L: 그러나 제사장 사독과 여호야다의 아들 브나야와 예언자 나단과 시므이와 레이와 다윗에게 [속한] 용사들은 아도니야와 함께하지 않았다.
ko.B: 그러나 제사장 사독과 여호야다의 아들 브나야와 예언자 나단과 시므이와 레이와 다윗의 용사들은 아도니야 편에 서지 않았다.
ko.R: 그러나 아도니야 편에 서지 않은 사람들도 있었다. 그들은 제사장 사독, 여호야다의 아들 브나야, 예언자 나단, 시므이, 레이, 그리고 다윗의 용사들이었다.

pt.L: Mas Zadoque, o sacerdote, e Benaia, filho de Joiada, e Natã, o profeta, e Simei, e Rei, e os valentes que [pertenciam] a Davi não estavam com Adonias.
pt.B: Mas o sacerdote Zadoque, Benaia, filho de Joiada, o profeta Natã, Simei, Rei e os guerreiros do próprio Davi não tomaram o partido de Adonias.
pt.R: Mas outros não se juntaram a Adonias. Eram eles o sacerdote Zadoque, Benaia, filho de Joiada, o profeta Natã, Simei, um homem chamado Rei, e os guerreiros do próprio Davi.

decisions.choice: Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet: titles of David's court
decisions.reason: Zadok served as priest beside Abiathar (2 Samuel 8:17; 15:24-29). Benaiah was over the king's foreign guard (2 Samuel 8:18; 23:20-23). Nathan was the prophet who brought God's word to David (2 Samuel 7; 12). Their names and titles are kept as the narrator gives them.

decisions.choice: Shimei and Rei: otherwise unknown men
decisions.reason: Neither man is named elsewhere in this role. This Shimei is probably not Shimei son of Gera, who cursed David (2 Samuel 16:5; 1 Kings 2:8). Some have suggested Rei is not a name, but the Hebrew lists it as one.

decisions.choice: the mighty men who belonged to David: his elite warriors
decisions.reason: These are the famous fighters of David's guard, listed in 2 Samuel 23:8-39.

decisions.choice: warriors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "warriors" for "mighty men", which here names a group of fighters.

decisions.choice: "los valientes" (L); "los guerreros" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "valientes", the word used for David's mighty men in 2 Samuel 23; Balanced and Readable say "guerreros", as the English says "warriors" (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: Shiméï, Réï
decisions.reason: French forms with the diaeresis for the separate vowel, as Shiméï in 2 Samuel; Benaya fils de Yehoyada, Sadok and Abiathar follow the French Samuel.

decisions.choice: "các dũng sĩ" (L); "các chiến binh" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the mighty men are David's elite fighters; "dũng sĩ" is the word used for them in 2 Samuel 23.

decisions.choice: "예언자" for *navi*
decisions.reason: As the Korean style guide and the Samuel note: the modern word, with the older church word as the alternative.

decisions.choice: Zadoque, Benaia filho de Joiada, Natã, Simei, Rei; um homem chamado Rei (R)
alternatives: Rei without explanation at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole book: David's officials keep the forms of 1 and 2 Samuel in Portuguese (2 Samuel 8:17-18; 12:1). "Rei" is a man's name (m2) that is also the Portuguese word for "king"; Literal and Balanced keep it as a name in a list of names, and Readable says "um homem chamado Rei" so that no reader takes it as a title. Literal keeps "Zadoque, o sacerdote" in the Hebrew order; Balanced and Readable put the title first, as 2 Samuel 7:2 does for "o profeta Natã".

decisions.choice: os valentes (L); os guerreiros (B, R)
decisions.reason: David's elite fighters (m3) are "os valentes" at Literal, the word of 2 Samuel 16:6 and 20:7 in Portuguese, and "os guerreiros" at Balanced and Readable, as the English says "warriors"; the same in verse 10.

source.text: וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח אֲדֹנִיָּ֗הוּ צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ וּמְרִ֔יא עִ֚ם אֶ֣בֶן הַזֹּחֶ֔לֶת אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֖צֶל עֵ֣ין רֹגֵ֑ל וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶת־כָּל־אֶחָיו֙ בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה עַבְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sacrificed Adonijah sheep and cattle and fatlings with [the] stone of the Zoheleth, which [is] beside En-rogel, and he invited all his brothers, sons of the king, and all [the] men of Judah, servants of the king.

en.L: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep and cattle and fattened cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, which [is] beside En-rogel; and he invited all his brothers, the sons of the king, and all the men of Judah, the servants of the king.
en.B: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle and fattened calves at the Stone of Zoheleth, near En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who were the king's officials.
en.R: Adonijah offered sheep, cattle and fat calves as sacrifices at the Stone of Zoheleth, near the spring of En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the other sons of the king. He also invited all the king's officials who came from the tribe of Judah.

es.L: Y sacrificó Adonías ovejas y bueyes y animales engordados junto a la piedra de Zohélet, que [está] al lado de En-roguel; e invitó a todos sus hermanos, los hijos del rey, y a todos los hombres de Judá, siervos del rey.
es.B: Adonías sacrificó ovejas, bueyes y becerros engordados junto a la Piedra de Zohélet, cerca de En-roguel. Invitó a todos sus hermanos, los hijos del rey, y a todos los hombres de Judá que eran oficiales del rey.
es.R: Adonías ofreció en sacrificio ovejas, bueyes y becerros gordos junto a la Piedra de Zohélet, cerca del manantial de En-roguel. Invitó a todos sus hermanos, los otros hijos del rey. También invitó a todos los oficiales del rey que eran de la tribu de Judá.

fr.L: Et Adonias sacrifia du petit bétail, et du gros bétail, et des bêtes grasses près de la pierre de Zohéleth, qui [est] à côté d’Èn-Roguel ; et il invita tous ses frères, les fils du roi, et tous les hommes de Juda, serviteurs du roi.
fr.B: Adonias offrit en sacrifice des moutons, des bœufs et des veaux gras à la Pierre de Zohéleth, près d’Èn-Roguel. Il invita tous ses frères, les fils du roi, et tous les hommes de Juda qui étaient officiers du roi.
fr.R: Adonias a offert des moutons, des bœufs et des veaux gras en sacrifice à la Pierre de Zohéleth, près de la source d’Èn-Roguel. Il a invité tous ses frères, les autres fils du roi. Il a aussi invité tous les officiers du roi qui venaient de la tribu de Juda.

sw.L: Adoniya akachinja kondoo na ng'ombe na ndama walionona karibu na jiwe la Zohelethi, lililo kando ya En-rogeli; akawaalika ndugu zake wote, wana wa mfalme, na watu wote wa Yuda, watumishi wa mfalme.
sw.B: Adoniya alitoa dhabihu ya kondoo, ng'ombe na ndama walionona kwenye Jiwe la Zohelethi, karibu na En-rogeli. Akawaalika ndugu zake wote, wana wa mfalme, na watu wote wa Yuda waliokuwa maafisa wa mfalme.
sw.R: Adoniya alitoa kondoo, ng'ombe na ndama wanono kuwa dhabihu kwenye Jiwe la Zohelethi, karibu na chemchemi ya En-rogeli. Akawaalika ndugu zake wote, wana wengine wa mfalme. Pia akawaalika maafisa wote wa mfalme waliotoka kabila la Yuda.

vi.L: A-đô-ni-gia giết chiên, bò và bò béo làm sinh tế bên tảng đá Xô-hê-lết, ở cạnh Ên-Rô-ghên; ông mời tất cả anh em mình, là các hoàng tử, và tất cả người Giu-đa, là các đầy tớ của vua.
vi.B: A-đô-ni-gia dâng chiên, bò và bê béo làm sinh tế tại Tảng Đá Xô-hê-lết, gần Ên-Rô-ghên. Ông mời tất cả anh em mình, là các hoàng tử, cùng tất cả những người Giu-đa làm quan trong triều vua.
vi.R: A-đô-ni-gia dâng chiên, bò và bê béo làm sinh tế tại Tảng Đá Xô-hê-lết, gần suối Ên-Rô-ghên. Ông mời tất cả anh em mình, là các con trai khác của vua. Ông cũng mời tất cả các quan chức của vua thuộc chi tộc Giu-đa.

ko.L: 그리고 아도니야가 엔로겔 곁에 있는 소헬렛 바위 옆에서 양과 소와 살진 송아지를 잡아 제사를 드렸다. 그리고 그는 자기 모든 형제, 곧 왕의 아들들과 왕의 신하인 유다의 모든 사람을 초대했다.
ko.B: 아도니야는 엔로겔 근처에 있는 소헬렛 바위에서 양과 소와 살진 송아지를 잡아 제사를 드렸다. 그는 자기 형제인 왕자들을 모두 초대하고, 왕의 신하로 있는 유다 사람들도 모두 불렀다.
ko.R: 아도니야는 엔로겔 샘 근처에 있는 소헬렛 바위에서 양과 소와 살진 송아지를 잡아 제물로 바쳤다. 그는 자기 형제들, 곧 다른 왕자들을 모두 초대했다. 또 유다 지파 출신인 왕의 신하들도 모두 초대했다.

pt.L: E Adonias sacrificou ovelhas, e bois, e gado gordo junto à pedra de Zoelete, que [está] ao lado de En-Rogel; e convidou todos os seus irmãos, os filhos do rei, e todos os homens de Judá, os servos do rei.
pt.B: Adonias sacrificou ovelhas, bois e bezerros gordos junto à Pedra de Zoelete, perto de En-Rogel. Convidou todos os seus irmãos, os filhos do rei, e todos os homens de Judá que eram oficiais do rei.
pt.R: Adonias ofereceu em sacrifício ovelhas, bois e bezerros gordos junto à Pedra de Zoelete, perto da fonte de Rogel. Ele convidou todos os seus irmãos, os outros filhos do rei. Convidou também todos os oficiais do rei que eram da tribo de Judá.

decisions.choice: sacrificed: slaughtered animals for a sacrificial feast
decisions.reason: The verb is used of sacrifices that were eaten by the worshipers in a feast. Such a feast marked a new king's rise (1 Samuel 11:15; 2 Samuel 15:12), so this was a public claim to the throne.

decisions.choice: the stone of Zoheleth beside En-rogel: a place just outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: En-rogel was a spring south-east of Jerusalem, where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet (Joshua 15:7; 2 Samuel 17:17). It lay below the city and out of sight of the palace, yet near enough to hear noise from the Gihon spring (verses 40-41). What the stone was is not known; its name may mean "the serpent stone" or "the sliding stone".

decisions.choice: the men of Judah, servants of the king: royal officials from Judah
decisions.reason: Adonijah was born at Hebron in Judah (2 Samuel 3:2-4), and he invited the officials from David's own tribe.

decisions.choice: the king's officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the spring of En-rogel
decisions.reason: Readable says what En-rogel was.

decisions.choice: "la piedra de Zohélet" (L), "la Piedra de Zohélet" (B, R); "En-roguel"
decisions.reason: En-roguel keeps the form of 2 Samuel 17:17 in Spanish; Zohélet is the usual Spanish spelling. Readable adds "manantial", as the English adds "spring" (r-en-2).

decisions.choice: la pierre (L) / la Pierre (B, R) de Zohéleth; Èn-Roguel
decisions.reason: French transcriptions; Èn-Roguel as in 2 Samuel 17:17.

decisions.choice: "các hoàng tử" for "the king's sons"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has a word for a king's sons; Readable keeps "các con trai khác của vua", as the English does, to say Adonijah was one of them.

decisions.choice: a pedra de Zoelete; En-Rogel (L, B); a fonte de Rogel (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "Zoelete" takes the final "-e" Portuguese adds after a consonant. The spring (m2) is "En-Rogel" at Literal and Balanced, the form of 2 Samuel 17:17 in Portuguese; since "En" is itself the Hebrew word for a spring, Readable says "a fonte de Rogel", as the English Readable says "the spring of En-rogel", without saying "spring" twice. Verse 25 at Readable names the place the same way.

source.text: וְֽאֶת־נָתָן֩ הַנָּבִ֨יא וּבְנָיָ֜הוּ וְאֶת־הַגִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וְאֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה אָחִ֖יו לֹ֥א קָרָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And Nathan the prophet and Benaiah and the mighty men and Solomon his brother not he invited.

en.L: But Nathan the prophet and Benaiah and the mighty men and Solomon his brother he did not invite.
en.B: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the warriors, or his brother Solomon.
en.R: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, David's warriors, or his brother Solomon.

es.L: Pero a Natán el profeta y a Benaía y a los valientes y a Salomón su hermano no invitó.
es.B: Pero no invitó al profeta Natán, ni a Benaía, ni a los guerreros, ni a su hermano Salomón.
es.R: Pero no invitó a Natán el profeta, ni a Benaía, ni a los guerreros de David, ni a su hermano Salomón.

fr.L: Mais Nathan le prophète, et Benaya, et les vaillants hommes, et Salomon son frère, il ne [les] invita pas.
fr.B: Mais il n’invita ni le prophète Nathan, ni Benaya, ni les guerriers, ni son frère Salomon.
fr.R: Mais il n’a invité ni le prophète Nathan, ni Benaya, ni les guerriers de David, ni son frère Salomon.

sw.L: Lakini Nathani nabii na Benaya na mashujaa na Sulemani ndugu yake hakuwaalika.
sw.B: Lakini hakumwalika Nathani nabii, wala Benaya, wala mashujaa, wala ndugu yake Sulemani.
sw.R: Lakini hakumwalika Nathani nabii, wala Benaya, wala mashujaa wa Daudi, wala ndugu yake Sulemani.

vi.L: Nhưng nhà tiên tri Na-than, Bê-na-gia, các dũng sĩ và Sa-lô-môn em mình thì ông không mời.
vi.B: Nhưng ông không mời nhà tiên tri Na-than, Bê-na-gia, các chiến binh, và Sa-lô-môn em mình.
vi.R: Nhưng ông không mời nhà tiên tri Na-than, Bê-na-gia, các chiến binh của Đa-vít, và Sa-lô-môn em mình.

ko.L: 그러나 예언자 나단과 브나야와 용사들과 그의 동생 솔로몬은 그가 초대하지 않았다.
ko.B: 그러나 그는 예언자 나단과 브나야와 용사들과 동생 솔로몬은 초대하지 않았다.
ko.R: 그러나 그는 예언자 나단과 브나야와 다윗의 용사들과 동생 솔로몬은 초대하지 않았다.

pt.L: Mas Natã, o profeta, e Benaia, e os valentes, e Salomão, o seu irmão, ele não convidou.
pt.B: Mas não convidou o profeta Natã, nem Benaia, nem os guerreiros, nem o seu irmão Salomão.
pt.R: Mas não convidou o profeta Natã, nem Benaia, nem os guerreiros de Davi, nem o seu irmão Salomão.

decisions.choice: the names come first: those left out
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the people first and the verb last, stressing who was not invited. They are the people who would stand for Solomon.

decisions.choice: Solomon his brother: his half-brother
decisions.reason: Solomon was David's son by Bathsheba (2 Samuel 12:24), so he and Adonijah had different mothers. Leaving him out shows that Adonijah saw him as a rival.

decisions.choice: David's warriors
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: "Sa-lô-môn em mình"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say which brother is older; Solomon was born after Adonijah (2 Samuel 3:4; 12:24), so he is "em".

decisions.choice: "동생"
decisions.reason: Korean must say whether a brother is older or younger. Solomon was born after Adonijah (2 Samuel 3:4; 5:14), so he is 동생.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נָתָ֗ן אֶל־בַּת־שֶׁ֤בַע אֵם־שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֣וֹא שָׁמַ֔עַתְּ כִּ֥י מָלַ֖ךְ אֲדֹנִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־חַגִּ֑ית וַאֲדֹנֵ֥ינוּ דָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Nathan to Bathsheba [the] mother of Solomon, saying, [is it] not [that] you have heard that has reigned Adonijah son of Haggith, and our lord David not knows?

en.L: And Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know [it]?
en.B: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, without our lord David knowing anything about it?
en.R: Then Nathan spoke to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. He said, "Have you heard? Adonijah, Haggith's son, has made himself king, and our master David does not even know about it!

es.L: Y habló Natán a Betsabé, madre de Salomón, diciendo: «¿No has oído que reina Adonías hijo de Haguit, y nuestro señor David no [lo] sabe?
es.B: Entonces Natán le dijo a Betsabé, la madre de Salomón: «¿No has oído que Adonías hijo de Haguit se ha hecho rey, sin que nuestro señor David sepa nada?
es.R: Entonces Natán fue a hablar con Betsabé, la madre de Salomón. Le dijo: «¿Ya te enteraste? ¡Adonías, el hijo de Haguit, se ha proclamado rey, y nuestro señor David ni siquiera lo sabe!

fr.L: Et Nathan dit à Bethsabée, mère de Salomon, disant : « N’as-tu pas entendu qu’Adonias fils de Haggith règne, et notre seigneur David ne [le] sait pas ?
fr.B: Alors Nathan dit à Bethsabée, la mère de Salomon : « N’as-tu pas appris qu’Adonias, fils de Haggith, est devenu roi sans que notre seigneur David le sache ?
fr.R: Alors Nathan est allé parler à Bethsabée, la mère de Salomon. Il lui a dit : « Tu es au courant ? Adonias, le fils de Haggith, s’est fait roi, et notre maître David ne le sait même pas !

sw.L: Nathani akamwambia Bathsheba mama yake Sulemani, akisema, "Je, hujasikia kwamba Adoniya mwana wa Hagithi ametawala, na bwana wetu Daudi hajui?
sw.B: Ndipo Nathani akamwambia Bathsheba, mama yake Sulemani, "Je, hujasikia kwamba Adoniya mwana wa Hagithi amekuwa mfalme, bila bwana wetu Daudi kujua lolote?
sw.R: Ndipo Nathani akasema na Bathsheba, mama yake Sulemani. Akamwambia, "Je, umesikia? Adoniya, mwana wa Hagithi, amejifanya mfalme, na bwana wetu Daudi hata hajui habari hiyo!

vi.L: Na-than nói với Bát-sê-ba, mẹ của Sa-lô-môn, rằng: "Bà chưa nghe sao, A-đô-ni-gia con trai Ha-ghít đã làm vua, mà Đa-vít chúa chúng ta không biết [điều đó]?
vi.B: Bấy giờ Na-than nói với Bát-sê-ba, mẹ của Sa-lô-môn: "Bà chưa nghe tin A-đô-ni-gia con trai Ha-ghít đã làm vua, mà Đa-vít chúa chúng ta không hay biết gì sao?
vi.R: Bấy giờ Na-than đến nói với Bát-sê-ba, mẹ của Sa-lô-môn: "Bà có nghe tin gì chưa? A-đô-ni-gia, con trai Ha-ghít, đã tự xưng làm vua, mà vua Đa-vít, chủ chúng ta, chẳng hay biết gì cả!

ko.L: 그러자 나단이 솔로몬의 어머니 밧세바에게 말했다. "학깃의 아들 아도니야가 왕이 되었는데, 우리 주 다윗께서는 알지 못하신다는 것을 듣지 못하셨습니까?
ko.B: 그때 나단이 솔로몬의 어머니 밧세바에게 말했다. "학깃의 아들 아도니야가 왕이 되었는데, 우리 주 다윗께서는 그 일을 전혀 모르고 계신다는 소식을 듣지 못하셨습니까?
ko.R: 그때 나단이 솔로몬의 어머니 밧세바를 찾아가 말했다. "소식을 들으셨습니까? 학깃의 아들 아도니야가 스스로 왕이 되었는데, 우리 주인이신 다윗께서는 그것을 알지도 못하십니다!

pt.L: E Natã disse a Bate-Seba, a mãe de Salomão, dizendo: "Você não ouviu que Adonias, filho de Hagite, se tornou rei, e o nosso senhor Davi não [o] sabe?
pt.B: Então Natã disse a Bate-Seba, mãe de Salomão: "Você não soube que Adonias, filho de Hagite, se tornou rei, sem que o nosso senhor Davi saiba de nada?
pt.R: Então Natã foi falar com Bate-Seba, a mãe de Salomão. Ele disse: "Você já soube? Adonias, filho de Hagite, se fez rei, e o nosso senhor Davi nem sabe disso!

decisions.choice: has become king: has claimed the kingship and acts as king
decisions.reason: The verb means "to reign, to become king". Adonijah had not been anointed, but his followers were already hailing him as king (verse 25).

decisions.choice: Bathsheba the mother of Solomon
decisions.reason: Bathsheba had been the wife of Uriah, and her son Solomon was born after David married her (2 Samuel 11:3, 27; 12:24). The narrator calls her by her tie to Solomon, the son whose life is at stake.

decisions.choice: son of Haggith: set against "mother of Solomon"
decisions.reason: The two princes are named by their mothers, which marks the rivalry between them.

decisions.choice: has made himself king
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Adonijah took the kingship for himself, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: our master David
decisions.reason: Readable says "master" for "lord" where it is not the full title "my lord the king".

decisions.choice: "reina" (L); "se ha hecho rey" (B); "se ha proclamado rey" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare verb "reign"; Balanced and Readable say that Adonijah has taken the title for himself, as the English Readable does (r-en-1). Readable keeps "nuestro señor": Spanish "señor" serves for the English "master" (r-en-2).

decisions.choice: notre maître David
decisions.reason: Readable says "maître" for "lord" where it is not the full title "mon seigneur le roi", as the English says "master" and as the French Samuel does.

decisions.choice: Nathan says "bà" to Bathsheba and "tôi" for himself
decisions.reason: Bathsheba is the king's wife and the mother of a prince; the prophet speaks to her with the respectful "bà", as she is called in the narration since 2 Samuel 12:24.

decisions.choice: "vua Đa-vít, chủ chúng ta" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable says "master" where it is not the full title; "chủ" is the plain word.

decisions.choice: Nathan and Bathsheba speak 합쇼체 to each other; Nathan calls her "부인" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks with respect to the king's wife and the mother of a king's son, and she answers in kind; the Hebrew gives no title, so Literal keeps none.

decisions.choice: Bate-Seba; você (Nathan to Bathsheba)
decisions.reason: "Bate-Seba" as 2 Samuel 11:3 in Portuguese, for the whole book. Nathan and Bathsheba speak to each other as people of the court, with "você", as people speak to each other throughout; the courtly third person is kept for the king. "O nosso senhor Davi" keeps "senhor" at every level, where the English Readable says "master".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה לְכִ֛י אִיעָצֵ֥ךְ נָ֖א עֵצָ֑ה וּמַלְּטִי֙ אֶת־נַפְשֵׁ֔ךְ וְאֶת־נֶ֥פֶשׁ בְּנֵ֖ךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now come, let me counsel you, please, counsel, and save your life and the life of your son Solomon.

en.L: And now come, let me counsel you, please, [with] counsel, and save your life and the life of your son Solomon.
en.B: Now come, let me give you some advice, so that you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
en.R: Now let me tell you what to do, so that you can save your life and your son Solomon's life.

es.L: Y ahora ven, déjame aconsejarte, te ruego, [con] consejo, y salva tu vida y la vida de tu hijo Salomón.
es.B: Ahora ven, déjame darte un consejo, para que puedas salvar tu vida y la de tu hijo Salomón.
es.R: Ahora déjame decirte lo que tienes que hacer, para que puedas salvar tu vida y la de tu hijo Salomón.

fr.L: Et maintenant viens, que je te conseille, je te prie, un conseil, et sauve ta vie et la vie de ton fils Salomon.
fr.B: Viens donc, je vais te donner un conseil, pour que tu sauves ta vie et celle de ton fils Salomon.
fr.R: Écoute ce que tu dois faire pour sauver ta vie et celle de ton fils Salomon.

sw.L: Basi sasa njoo, tafadhali nikushauri shauri, uokoe maisha yako na maisha ya mwanao Sulemani.
sw.B: Basi sasa njoo, nikupe shauri, ili uokoe maisha yako mwenyewe na maisha ya mwanao Sulemani.
sw.R: Basi sasa nikuambie la kufanya, ili uokoe maisha yako na maisha ya mwanao Sulemani.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, hãy đến, xin để tôi bàn cho bà một lời bàn, để bà cứu mạng sống mình và mạng sống của Sa-lô-môn con trai bà.
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, xin bà hãy nghe tôi góp ý, để bà cứu được mạng sống của mình và của Sa-lô-môn con trai bà.
vi.R: Bây giờ, tôi xin chỉ cho bà phải làm gì để cứu mạng bà và mạng Sa-lô-môn, con trai bà.

ko.L: 그러니 이제 오십시오. 제가 부디 당신에게 조언을 하겠습니다. 그래서 당신의 목숨과 당신의 아들 솔로몬의 목숨을 구하십시오.
ko.B: 이제 제가 부인께 조언을 드리겠습니다. 그러면 부인의 목숨과 아드님 솔로몬의 목숨을 구하실 수 있을 것입니다.
ko.R: 제가 어떻게 하셔야 할지 말씀드리겠습니다. 그러면 부인과 아드님 솔로몬의 목숨을 구하실 수 있습니다.

pt.L: E agora venha, deixe-me, por favor, aconselhá-la [com] um conselho, e salve a sua vida e a vida do seu filho Salomão.
pt.B: Agora venha, deixe-me lhe dar um conselho, para que você salve a sua vida e a vida do seu filho Salomão.
pt.R: Agora deixe-me dizer o que você deve fazer para salvar a sua vida e a vida do seu filho Salomão.

decisions.choice: and save: so that you may save
decisions.reason: The second command gives the purpose of the first: follow the advice, and you will save your lives.

decisions.choice: save your life and your son's: a rival's family was in danger
decisions.reason: A new king often put to death those who could claim the throne, together with their families (15:29; 2 Kings 10:6-11; 11:1). Bathsheba says the same in verse 21.

decisions.choice: let me tell you what to do
decisions.reason: Readable says "counsel you ... counsel" in plain words.

source.text: לְכִ֞י וּבֹ֣אִי׀אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וְאָמַ֤רְתְּ אֵלָיו֙ הֲלֹֽא־אַתָּ֞ה אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ נִשְׁבַּ֤עְתָּ לַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי־שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בְנֵךְ֙ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרַ֔י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְאִ֑י וּמַדּ֖וּעַ מָלַ֥ךְ אֲדֹנִיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Go and enter to the king David and say to him, [did] not you, my lord the king, swear to your maidservant, saying, that Solomon your son will reign after me and he will sit on my throne? And why has reigned Adonijah?

en.L: Go and go in to King David and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your maidservant, saying, "Surely Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne"? Then why has Adonijah become king?'
en.B: Go in to King David and say to him, 'My lord the king, did you not swear to your servant, "Your son Solomon will be king after me, and he will sit on my throne"? So why has Adonijah become king?'
en.R: Go in to King David and say to him, 'Your Majesty, did you not make a promise to me? You said, "Your son Solomon will be king after me. He will sit on my throne." So why has Adonijah become king?'

es.L: Ve y entra al rey David y dile: “¿No juraste tú, mi señor el rey, a tu sierva, diciendo: ‘Ciertamente Salomón tu hijo reinará después de mí, y él se sentará en mi trono’? ¿Por qué, pues, reina Adonías?”.
es.B: Entra a ver al rey David y dile: “Mi señor el rey, ¿no le juraste a tu sierva: ‘Tu hijo Salomón será rey después de mí, y él se sentará en mi trono’? ¿Por qué, entonces, se ha hecho rey Adonías?”.
es.R: Entra a ver al rey David y dile: “Mi rey, ¿no me hiciste una promesa? Me dijiste: ‘Tu hijo Salomón será rey después de mí. Él se sentará en mi trono’. ¿Por qué, entonces, se ha hecho rey Adonías?”.

fr.L: Va, et entre chez le roi David, et dis-lui : “N’as-tu pas, mon seigneur le roi, juré à ta servante, disant : ‘Certainement Salomon ton fils régnera après moi, et lui s’assiéra sur mon trône’ ? Et pourquoi Adonias règne-t-il ?”
fr.B: Va trouver le roi David et dis-lui : “Mon seigneur le roi, n’as-tu pas juré à ta servante : ‘Ton fils Salomon sera roi après moi, et c’est lui qui s’assiéra sur mon trône’ ? Pourquoi donc Adonias est-il devenu roi ?”
fr.R: Va voir le roi David et dis-lui : “Ô roi, ne m’as-tu pas fait une promesse ? Tu m’as dit : ‘Ton fils Salomon sera roi après moi. C’est lui qui s’assiéra sur mon trône.’ Alors pourquoi est-ce Adonias qui est devenu roi ?”

sw.L: Nenda uingie kwa mfalme Daudi umwambie, 'Je, wewe, bwana wangu mfalme, hukumwapia mjakazi wako, ukisema, "Hakika Sulemani mwanao atatawala baada yangu, naye ataketi juu ya kiti changu cha enzi"? Basi kwa nini Adoniya ametawala?'
sw.B: Nenda uingie kwa mfalme Daudi umwambie, 'Bwana wangu mfalme, je, hukumwapia mtumishi wako, "Mwanao Sulemani atakuwa mfalme baada yangu, naye ataketi juu ya kiti changu cha enzi"? Basi kwa nini Adoniya amekuwa mfalme?'
sw.R: Nenda kwa mfalme Daudi umwambie, 'Mtukufu mfalme, je, hukuniahidi? Ulisema, "Mwanao Sulemani atakuwa mfalme baada yangu. Ataketi juu ya kiti changu cha enzi." Basi kwa nini Adoniya amekuwa mfalme?'

vi.L: Hãy đi vào gặp vua Đa-vít và nói với vua: 'Thưa chúa tôi là vua, chẳng phải vua đã thề với tớ gái của vua rằng: "Chắc chắn Sa-lô-môn con trai ngươi sẽ làm vua sau ta, và nó sẽ ngồi trên ngai ta" sao? Vậy tại sao A-đô-ni-gia lại làm vua?'
vi.B: Bà hãy vào gặp vua Đa-vít và tâu: 'Tâu bệ hạ, chẳng phải bệ hạ đã thề với tớ gái của bệ hạ rằng: "Sa-lô-môn con trai bà sẽ làm vua sau ta, và nó sẽ ngồi trên ngai ta" sao? Vậy sao A-đô-ni-gia lại lên làm vua?'
vi.R: Bà hãy vào gặp vua Đa-vít và thưa: 'Thưa đức vua, chẳng phải đức vua đã hứa với tôi sao? Đức vua đã nói: "Sa-lô-môn con trai bà sẽ làm vua sau ta. Nó sẽ ngồi trên ngai ta." Vậy sao A-đô-ni-gia lại lên làm vua?'

ko.L: 다윗 왕에게 가서 들어가 그에게 말씀하십시오. '내 주 임금님, 임금님께서 임금님의 여종에게 "반드시 당신의 아들 솔로몬이 나를 이어 왕이 되고, 그가 내 왕좌에 앉을 것이오" 하고 맹세하지 않으셨습니까? 그런데 어찌하여 아도니야가 왕이 되었습니까?'
ko.B: 다윗 왕에게 들어가서 이렇게 말씀하십시오. '내 주 임금님, 임금님께서는 이 여종에게 "당신의 아들 솔로몬이 나를 이어 왕이 되고, 내 왕좌에 앉을 것이오" 하고 맹세하지 않으셨습니까? 그런데 어찌하여 아도니야가 왕이 되었습니까?'
ko.R: 다윗 왕에게 들어가서 이렇게 말씀드리십시오. '임금님, 임금님께서 저에게 약속하지 않으셨습니까? "당신의 아들 솔로몬이 나를 이어 왕이 될 것이오. 그가 내 왕좌에 앉을 것이오" 하고 말씀하셨습니다. 그런데 왜 아도니야가 왕이 되었습니까?'

pt.L: Vá e entre até o rei Davi e diga-lhe: 'Não jurou o senhor, meu senhor, o rei, à sua serva, dizendo: "Certamente Salomão, o seu filho, reinará depois de mim, e ele se sentará no meu trono"? Por que, então, Adonias se tornou rei?'
pt.B: Vá falar com o rei Davi e diga-lhe: 'Meu senhor, o rei, o senhor não jurou à sua serva: "O seu filho Salomão será rei depois de mim, e ele se sentará no meu trono"? Por que, então, Adonias se tornou rei?'
pt.R: Vá falar com o rei Davi e diga a ele: 'Majestade, o senhor não me fez uma promessa? O senhor disse: "O seu filho Salomão será rei depois de mim. Ele vai se sentar no meu trono." Então por que Adonias se tornou rei?'

decisions.choice: your maidservant: Bathsheba's polite way of speaking of herself
decisions.reason: Bathsheba calls herself the king's *'amah*, his female servant, as a polite way of speaking of herself before him (2 Samuel 14:12, 15). It is the language of respect at court, not a statement about her rank.

decisions.choice: the oath to Bathsheba: a promise not told earlier
decisions.reason: The books of Samuel do not record this oath. They tell that the LORD loved Solomon (2 Samuel 12:24-25), and 1 Chronicles 22:9-10 tells of a promise about him. David does not deny the oath in verse 30.

decisions.choice: surely: the word that opens the words of an oath
decisions.reason: The small word that introduces the oath gives its content and makes it emphatic.

decisions.choice: your maidservant
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the feminine form, as in 2 Samuel 14.

decisions.choice: your servant (Balanced); me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the polite self-reference as "your servant"; Readable may say "me", as the books of Samuel do.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: "tu sierva" (L, B); "me" (R)
decisions.reason: Bathsheba speaks of herself as "tu sierva", the Samuel notes' word for a woman's polite self-reference to the king, at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "me", as the English Readable says "me" (r-en-2).

decisions.choice: ta servante (L, B); me (R)
decisions.reason: French "servante" serves for both Literal and Balanced, where the English varies "maidservant" and "servant"; Readable says "me", as the English does.

decisions.choice: « », then “ ”, then ‘ ’
decisions.reason: Nathan quotes the words Bathsheba is to say, and she quotes David's oath: French marks the three levels of speech with « », “ ” and ‘ ’, as the French Samuel does.

decisions.choice: mjakazi wako (Literal); mtumishi wako (Balanced); -ni- (me, Readable)
decisions.reason: Bathsheba's polite self-reference: Literal keeps the feminine "mjakazi wako" (your maidservant), Balanced the polite "mtumishi wako", Readable the plain first person, as the Swahili of 2 Samuel 14.

decisions.choice: "tớ gái của vua" (L); "tớ gái của bệ hạ" (B); "tôi" (R)
decisions.reason: The Kings terms note gives "tớ gái của vua" for a woman's polite self-reference before the king; Readable says "tôi", as the English Readable says "me".

decisions.choice: the king says "ta" and "bà" to Bathsheba
decisions.reason: David speaks as king ("ta"), but to his wife and the mother of his son Vietnamese cannot use the "ngươi" he uses to officials; "bà" fits her age and rank (uncertain).

decisions.choice: Bathsheba calls herself "임금님의 여종" (L), "이 여종" (B), "저" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel note for "your servant" to the king: the humble self-reference at Literal and Balanced, plain "저" at Readable, as the English Readable says "me".

decisions.choice: David speaks to Bathsheba in 하오체 with "당신", here and wherever his oath is quoted
decisions.reason: The king speaks to his wife with the respectful 하오체 of a king to a queen; Genesis gives husband and wife 당신, kept here.

decisions.choice: a sua serva (L, B); me (R)
decisions.reason: Bathsheba's polite way of speaking of herself (m1) is "a sua serva" at Literal and Balanced, as the woman of Tekoa says it in 2 Samuel 14:12 in Portuguese; Readable says "me", as the English does. The same in verse 17.

decisions.choice: Certamente
decisions.reason: The word that opens the words of the oath (m3) is "certamente" at Literal, which gives the oath its force, as the English "Surely"; the same in verses 17 and 30.

source.text: הִנֵּ֗ה עוֹדָ֛ךְ מְדַבֶּ֥רֶת שָׁ֖ם עִם־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאֲנִי֙ אָב֣וֹא אַחֲרַ֔יִךְ וּמִלֵּאתִ֖י אֶת־דְּבָרָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, still you speaking there with the king, and I will come after you and I will fill your words.

en.L: Look, while you [are] still speaking there with the king, I will come in after you and fill up your words."
en.B: Then, while you are still there talking to the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words."
en.R: While you are still talking with the king, I will come in and tell him that what you said is true."

es.L: He aquí, mientras tú todavía [estés] hablando allí con el rey, yo entraré tras de ti y completaré tus palabras».
es.B: Y mientras tú todavía estés allí hablando con el rey, yo entraré después de ti y confirmaré tus palabras».
es.R: Mientras todavía estés hablando con el rey, yo entraré y le diré que lo que tú dices es verdad».

fr.L: Voici, pendant que tu [seras] encore là à parler avec le roi, moi, j’entrerai après toi, et je compléterai tes paroles. »
fr.B: Et pendant que tu seras encore là à parler avec le roi, j’entrerai à mon tour et je confirmerai tes paroles. »
fr.R: Pendant que tu parleras encore avec le roi, j’arriverai et je lui dirai que tes paroles sont vraies. »

sw.L: Tazama, ungali ukisema huko na mfalme, nami nitaingia nyuma yako na kuyajaza maneno yako."
sw.B: Kisha, ukiwa bado unazungumza na mfalme huko, nitaingia nyuma yako na kuyathibitisha maneno yako."
sw.R: Ukiwa bado unazungumza na mfalme, nitaingia na kumwambia kwamba uliyosema ni kweli."

vi.L: Kìa, trong khi bà còn đang nói ở đó với vua, tôi sẽ vào sau bà và làm đầy những lời bà nói."
vi.B: Rồi trong khi bà còn đang tâu chuyện với vua, tôi sẽ vào sau và xác nhận lời bà nói."
vi.R: Trong khi bà còn đang nói chuyện với vua, tôi sẽ vào và thưa với vua rằng lời bà nói là đúng."

ko.L: 보십시오, 당신이 아직 거기서 왕과 말씀하고 계실 때에, 제가 당신의 뒤를 따라 들어가서 당신의 말을 채우겠습니다."
ko.B: 부인께서 아직 거기서 임금님과 말씀을 나누고 계실 때, 제가 뒤따라 들어가서 부인의 말씀이 옳다고 확인해 드리겠습니다."
ko.R: 부인께서 임금님과 이야기하고 계실 때, 제가 들어가서 부인의 말씀이 사실이라고 임금님께 말씀드리겠습니다."

pt.L: Eis que, enquanto você ainda [estiver] falando ali com o rei, eu entrarei depois de você e completarei as suas palavras."
pt.B: Então, enquanto você ainda estiver ali falando com o rei, eu entrarei depois de você e confirmarei as suas palavras."
pt.R: Enquanto você ainda estiver falando com o rei, eu vou entrar e dizer a ele que o que você disse é verdade."

decisions.choice: fill up your words: confirm them
decisions.reason: To "fill" someone's words is to complete and back them up. A second witness makes the report stand (Deuteronomy 19:15).

decisions.choice: tell him that what you said is true
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: "làm đầy những lời bà nói" (L); "xác nhận lời bà nói" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of filling up someone's words; Balanced says what it means, and Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: completarei as suas palavras
decisions.reason: "Encher as palavras" would not be understood; "completar" keeps the picture of filling up what is lacking and already points to the sense of backing up her report (m1).

source.text: וַתָּבֹ֨א בַת־שֶׁ֤בֶע אֶל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַחַ֔דְרָה וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ זָקֵ֣ן מְאֹ֑ד וַֽאֲבִישַׁג֙ הַשּׁ֣וּנַמִּ֔ית מְשָׁרַ֖ת אֶת־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Bathsheba to the king to the room, and the king [was] old very, and Abishag the Shunammite [was] serving the king.

en.L: And Bathsheba went in to the king, to the inner room; and the king [was] very old, and Abishag the Shunammite [was] serving the king.
en.B: So Bathsheba went in to the king in his room. He was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was attending him.
en.R: So Bathsheba went to see the king in his bedroom. He was very old, and Abishag from Shunem was taking care of him.

es.L: Y Betsabé entró al rey, a la alcoba; y el rey [era] muy viejo, y Abisag la sunamita servía al rey.
es.B: Betsabé entró, pues, a ver al rey en su habitación. Él era muy viejo, y Abisag la sunamita lo atendía.
es.R: Betsabé fue a ver al rey en su dormitorio. Él era muy anciano, y Abisag, la de Sunem, lo cuidaba.

fr.L: Et Bethsabée entra chez le roi, dans la chambre ; et le roi [était] très vieux, et Abishag la Shounamite servait le roi.
fr.B: Bethsabée se rendit donc chez le roi, dans sa chambre. Il était très vieux, et Abishag la Shounamite était à son service.
fr.R: Bethsabée est donc allée voir le roi dans sa chambre. Il était très vieux, et Abishag, la jeune fille de Shounem, s’occupait de lui.

sw.L: Bathsheba akaingia kwa mfalme, chumbani; na mfalme [alikuwa] mzee sana, na Abishagi Mshunami [alikuwa] akimhudumia mfalme.
sw.B: Basi Bathsheba akaingia kwa mfalme chumbani mwake. Mfalme alikuwa mzee sana, na Abishagi Mshunami alikuwa akimhudumia.
sw.R: Basi Bathsheba akaenda kumwona mfalme chumbani mwake mwa kulala. Mfalme alikuwa mzee sana, na Abishagi wa Shunemu alikuwa akimtunza.

vi.L: Bát-sê-ba đi vào gặp vua trong phòng; vua [đã] rất già, và A-bi-sác người Su-nem [đang] hầu hạ vua.
vi.B: Vậy Bát-sê-ba vào gặp vua trong phòng riêng. Vua đã rất già, và A-bi-sác người Su-nem đang hầu hạ vua.
vi.R: Vậy Bát-sê-ba vào phòng ngủ của vua. Vua đã rất già, và A-bi-sác người Su-nem đang chăm sóc vua.

ko.L: 그리고 밧세바가 왕에게로, 그 내실로 들어갔다. 그리고 왕은 매우 늙었고, 수넴 여자 아비삭이 왕을 섬기고 [있었다].
ko.B: 그래서 밧세바는 왕의 방으로 들어갔다. 왕은 매우 늙었고, 수넴 여자 아비삭이 그를 시중들고 있었다.
ko.R: 그래서 밧세바는 왕을 만나러 침실로 들어갔다. 왕은 아주 늙었고, 수넴에서 온 아비삭이 그를 돌보고 있었다.

pt.L: E Bate-Seba entrou até o rei, no aposento; e o rei [estava] muito velho, e Abisague, a sunamita, [estava] servindo o rei.
pt.B: Então Bate-Seba foi ao quarto do rei. Ele estava muito velho, e Abisague, a sunamita, o servia.
pt.R: Então Bate-Seba foi ver o rei no quarto dele. Ele estava muito velho, e Abisague, de Suném, estava cuidando dele.

decisions.choice: the inner room: the king's private room
decisions.reason: The word names an inner room of a house, often a bedroom (2 Samuel 13:10). The king no longer leaves his bed (verse 47).

decisions.choice: the king was very old, and Abishag was serving him: the scene Bathsheba walks into
decisions.reason: These clauses pause the story to show what Bathsheba sees: an old man in bed and a young woman tending him.

decisions.choice: bedroom
decisions.reason: Readable names the kind of room.

source.text: וַתִּקֹּ֣ד בַּת־שֶׁ֔בַע וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה־לָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And bowed Bathsheba and bowed down to the king, and said the king, what to you?

en.L: And Bathsheba bowed and bowed down to the king; and the king said, "What [is it] for you?"
en.B: Bathsheba bowed low before the king, and the king asked, "What do you want?"
en.R: Bathsheba bowed down in front of the king. The king asked, "What can I do for you?"

es.L: E hizo reverencia Betsabé y se postró ante el rey; y el rey dijo: «¿Qué [es] para ti?».
es.B: Betsabé se inclinó profundamente ante el rey, y el rey le preguntó: «¿Qué quieres?».
es.R: Betsabé se inclinó delante del rey. El rey le preguntó: «¿Qué puedo hacer por ti?».

fr.L: Et Bethsabée s’inclina et se prosterna devant le roi ; et le roi dit : « Qu’[as]-tu ? »
fr.B: Bethsabée s’inclina profondément devant le roi, et le roi lui demanda : « Que veux-tu ? »
fr.R: Bethsabée s’est inclinée devant le roi. Le roi lui a demandé : « Que puis-je faire pour toi ? »

sw.L: Bathsheba akainama, akamsujudia mfalme; mfalme akasema, "Una nini?"
sw.B: Bathsheba akainama sana mbele ya mfalme, naye mfalme akauliza, "Unataka nini?"
sw.R: Bathsheba akainama mbele ya mfalme. Mfalme akamwuliza, "Nikusaidie nini?"

vi.L: Bát-sê-ba cúi mình và quỳ lạy vua; vua nói: "Bà [muốn] gì?"
vi.B: Bát-sê-ba cúi rạp mình trước mặt vua. Vua hỏi: "Bà muốn gì?"
vi.R: Bát-sê-ba quỳ xuống lạy vua. Vua hỏi: "Ta có thể làm gì cho bà?"

ko.L: 그리고 밧세바가 몸을 굽혀 왕에게 절했다. 그러자 왕이 말했다. "당신에게 무슨 [일이오]?"
ko.B: 밧세바가 왕 앞에 몸을 굽혀 절하자, 왕이 물었다. "무엇을 원하오?"
ko.R: 밧세바가 왕 앞에 엎드려 절했다. 왕이 물었다. "내가 당신에게 무엇을 해 주면 좋겠소?"

pt.L: E Bate-Seba se inclinou e se prostrou diante do rei; e o rei disse: "Que [há] com você?"
pt.B: Bate-Seba se curvou profundamente diante do rei, e o rei perguntou: "O que você deseja?"
pt.R: Bate-Seba se curvou diante do rei. O rei perguntou: "O que posso fazer por você?"

decisions.choice: bowed and bowed down: deep reverence before the king
decisions.reason: Two verbs together describe bowing the head and then lying face down, the full honor given to a king.

decisions.choice: What is it for you?: What do you want?
decisions.reason: The short question asks what she has come to request.

decisions.choice: bowed low (Balanced); bowed down (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two verbs into one.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אֲדֹנִי֙ אַתָּ֨ה נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתָּ בַּֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ לַֽאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי־שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֵ֖ךְ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרָ֑י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסְאִֽי׃
